# CodeSparring

> CodeSparring is a coding interview practice platform for software engineers and data engineers.
> It combines free public Python, Data Engineering, and System Design lessons with AI-led coding,
> real-codebase debugging, and system design interviews. Candidates practice explaining their
> reasoning, working through problems, and learning from session feedback.

Canonical website: https://www.codesparring.dev. Last reviewed: 2026-10-15.

Public lesson reading and sample feedback do not require an account. Graded lesson workspaces,
saved sessions, and personalized feedback require sign-in; the interview room also offers a
limited guest trial. Next-practice recommendations after an interview are available to free and
paid accounts. Interview allowances and paid features are separate; consult the live pricing page
for current prices, quotas, and availability rather than inferring unlimited free interviews.

Public lessons use `/learn/{track}/{levelSlug}/{lessonId}`. Cite the reading page, not its
authenticated `/workspace` child. The legacy `/learn/sql` URLs redirect to Data Engineering.
Interview practice supports voice or text, with executable coding tasks where the selected runner
supports the language. Feedback is practice guidance, not a hiring decision or a job guarantee.

## Product and access

- [Homepage](https://www.codesparring.dev): overview of interview practice and the public curriculum.
- [Pricing and access](https://www.codesparring.dev/pricing): current free-account allowances, Pro features, and subscription prices.
- [AI coding interview practice](https://www.codesparring.dev/ai-coding-interview-practice): explain an approach, write code, run tests, and receive session feedback.
- [Real-codebase debugging practice](https://www.codesparring.dev/bug-fix-interview-practice): reproduce a failure, inspect files, form a hypothesis, patch, and verify. Python practice includes a four-module cache cleanup incident with a follow-up feature task.
- [System design interview practice](https://www.codesparring.dev/system-design-interview-practice): rehearse architecture discussions and explain tradeoffs.
- [Sample feedback](https://www.codesparring.dev/samples): public examples of scored session reports, without starting an interview.
- [Free interview access](https://www.codesparring.dev/free-ai-coding-interview): guest-trial and free-account entry points.
- [Roadmap preview](https://www.codesparring.dev/roadmap/preview): preview of a personalized interview preparation plan; see pricing for access.

## Free public curriculum

- [Learn hub](https://www.codesparring.dev/learn): Python, Data Engineering, and System Design course entry points.
- [All lessons](https://www.codesparring.dev/learn/all): flat index of public reading pages.
- [Python course](https://www.codesparring.dev/learn/python): fundamentals, Python idioms, applied development, engineering, testing, and code review.
- [Data Engineering course](https://www.codesparring.dev/learn/data-engineering): SQL, modeling, data quality, cloud data, warehouses, batch pipelines, streaming, distributed compute, and data for AI.
- [System Design course](https://www.codesparring.dev/learn/system-design): interview method, networking, storage, scaling, distributed systems, event-driven systems, reliability, and security.

## Selected lessons

- [HTTP semantics](https://www.codesparring.dev/learn/system-design/foundations/sd-l1-http-semantics): method safety, idempotency, status codes, conditional requests, and caching.
- [HTTP versions](https://www.codesparring.dev/learn/system-design/foundations/sd-l1-http-versions): HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 tradeoffs.
- [Delivery semantics](https://www.codesparring.dev/learn/system-design/event-driven/sd-l6-delivery-semantics): at-most-once and at-least-once delivery, idempotency, and effectively-once effects.
- [Retries, DLQs, and backpressure](https://www.codesparring.dev/learn/system-design/event-driven/sd-l6-retries-dlq-backpressure): transient failures, retry topics, poison messages, consumer lag, and bounded work.
- [Leader election and fencing](https://www.codesparring.dev/learn/system-design/distributed-core/sd-l5-leader-election-fencing): leases, fencing tokens, split brain, and stale leaders.
